names.official: Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

summary: Macao runs its own liberal entry regime, separate from mainland China: EU and many other passports get 90 visa-free days (British citizens six months), dozens of nationalities get 30, and most of the rest can buy a visa on arrival at the border — only a handful of passports must apply in advance.

currencyLimits.text: Arriving travelers carrying cash or bearer negotiable instruments (traveler's checks, cheques, money orders) worth MOP 120,000 (about USD 15,000) or more must declare them to customs and use the red channel. On departure, declare truthfully if a customs officer asks. Transit passengers are exempt.

notes: Macao Customs lets each passenger bring in, without declaring it, up to 19 cigarettes, 1 cigar (of no more than 3 g) and 25 g of leaf tobacco, and 1 litre of drinks over 30% alcohol; declare anything beyond these quantities.
Canada's travel advice says it is prohibited to import, export or distribute e-cigarettes, vaporizers and their refills in Macao, and that offenders can expect heavy fines.

payments.text: Australia's Smartraveller says credit cards are widely accepted in Macao and some shops also accept Hong Kong dollars and Chinese yuan; the Government of Canada also says Hong Kong dollars are accepted.

safety.text: The UK FCDO says crime levels are low but pickpocketing and other street crime does happen, and advises taking particular care of valuables in crowded areas and when visiting casinos late at night.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Macau?
faq.answer: Most travelers do not: EU and several dozen other passports enter visa-free for 90 days (British citizens for six months), and nationalities including the US, Canada, Australia, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand get 30 days. Most remaining nationalities can buy a visa on arrival (MOP 200) at the border — only a handful, such as Bangladesh, Nepal, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Vietnam, must obtain a visa in advance through Chinese diplomatic missions.

faq.question: Is Macau covered by a Chinese visa?
faq.answer: Macao's Public Security Police sets its own entry rules: its own list of visa-exempt nationalities, a visa on arrival, and visas obtained through Chinese diplomatic missions for the nationalities that need one in advance. No official source we could read states how a mainland Chinese visa applies to Macao.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Macau?
faq.answer: US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 30 days. EU citizens get 90 days, and British citizens up to six months.

faq.question: Can I do a day trip to Macau from Hong Kong?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes day trips. Macao's Public Security Police lists the Outer Harbour Ferry Terminal and the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge among its border checkpoints, and Hong Kong permanent residents can enter with their Hong Kong Permanent Identity Card.

faq.question: How does the Macau visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: Eligible nationalities pay for the visa at the border checkpoint — MOP 200, or MOP 100 for children under 12 — and are granted a stay of up to 30 days; MOP 300 buys multiple entries within that stay. Nationalities excluded from the scheme must apply in advance through a Chinese embassy or consulate.
